description: tests/test-prop19-real-content-hook.sh's states (a) and (b) assert only `rc -eq 0` for 'the wake completes' plus draft.md's own content -- they never assert `last_wake_result` in STATE.md (DRAFT vs ABORTED). This is a near-tautological check given run.sh's own documented design: run.sh returns rc=0 for EVERY legitimate outcome including ABORTED (run.sh lines 20-23, 196-209), so `rc -eq 0` cannot discriminate 'the real-content hook worked AND the wake actually reached a DRAFT/PUBLISHED state' from 'the real-content hook worked but the wake silently ABORTED downstream'. Concretely: state (a)'s own fixture file is exactly 3 lines (heading, blank, one content line) -- gates/v0.sh's real (non-FORCE) check requires `line_count -gt 3` (gates/v0.sh line 38), so this exact fixture FAILS the real V0 gate; and no ARTICLE_JUDGE_V05_RESPONSE is supplied in this test, so gates/v05.sh's real (a)-(d) fail closed to false (gates/v05.sh lines 88-100) and V0.5 also fails. Since ARTICLE_TEST_V0_RESULTS/ARTICLE_TEST_V05_RESULTS are unset here (test only sets ARTICLE_TEST=1... unset variables, real-mode path, so run.sh invokes the REAL non-forced gates, lines 173-179), a real run of this exact fixture would exhaust all 3 retry rounds and ABORT the wake -- yet the test's only pass condition (`rc -eq 0`) is satisfied identically whether the wake reaches DRAFT or silently ABORTS. The test's own success message ('real-mode wake with real draft supplied completes, rc=0') therefore overstates what was actually verified.

evidence.snippet:
OUT="$(ARTICLE_DIR="$T" AUTONOMY=off ARTICLE_REAL_TOPIC="x402" ARTICLE_REAL_RESEARCH=sufficient ARTICLE_REAL_DRAFT_PATH="$FIXTURE" bash "$SKILL/run.sh" 2>&1)"; rc=$?
ok "$([ $rc -eq 0 ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" "real-mode wake with real draft supplied completes, rc=0 (rc=$rc): $OUT"
... (no assertion anywhere on STATE.md's last_wake_result)

additionalEvidence.description: Line 38: real V0 requires line_count -gt 3; the test's own 3-line fixture fails this.
